heading: Adaptive optimizers can generalize worse than SGD under limited tuning
definition: on image-classification and language benchmarks, adaptive methods such as Adam often reach worse held-out performance than SGD or momentum SGD when only learning rates and decay schedules are tuned, sometimes despite equal or better training performance (Wilson et al. 2017). Broader tuning can remove or reverse the difference (Choi et al. 2019), decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD can recover it (Loshchilov & Hutter 2019; Keskar & Socher 2017), and on word-level language models Adam can do better.
summary: A WRN-40-4 study reports lower training loss but worse test accuracy with Adam; a replication reproduces the CIFAR-10 gap but finds the opposite optimizer ranking for a character-LSTM on War and Peace. Tuning only the training schedule removes the gap for VGG on CIFAR-10, while pretraining LLaMA on C4 at the 1B scale favors Adam.

suggested_status.by_scale: C at <1B, with R2 evidence for recipe-specific deficits; ? at 1-10B, where language-model scope limits do not establish reproduction of the penalty. counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size has no 10-100B or >100B coverage.
suggested_status.reason: A failed replication warrants C while conditional deficits remain independently reproduced. The replication reproduces the CIFAR-10 VGG deficit but reverses the War and Peace character-LSTM ordering; Table 5 labels both original and replication results as validation loss, so an evaluation-split change is not established (arXiv:2002.11803#R4, arXiv:2002.11803#R8). Independently, WRN-40-4/CIFAR-100 shows lower Adam training loss alongside worse test accuracy (arXiv:1705.07774#R2, arXiv:1705.07774#R3). Choi's original tuning comparison finds that schedule tuning alone removes its CIFAR-10/VGG separation, qualifying the stated tuning restriction (arXiv:1910.05446#R1, arXiv:1910.05446#R3). At 1B, C4 LLaMA pretraining favors Adam, extending the language-model exception without reproducing the penalty (arXiv:2605.17787#R7, arXiv:2605.17787#R8). counts: versions.V4.verdicts records supporting, scope-limiting and challenging evidence; these overlapping categories do not establish how often the effect occurs.
suggested_status.open_questions: Would independent, equal-budget restricted-versus-expanded tuning comparisons reproduce the deficit with matched architectures, evaluation splits, checkpoint rules and paired training measurements? A defined workload sample would test 'often'; matched comparisons at 1-10B would clarify scale transfer.

source.title: The Marginal Value of Adaptive Gradient Methods in Machine Learning
source.authors: Ashia C. Wilson; R. Roelofs; Mitchell Stern; N. Srebro; B. Recht

original_result.setup: Wilson et al. compared optimizers on CIFAR-10 using VGG with batch normalization and dropout, tuning learning rates and decay schedules while keeping other optimizer parameters at defaults.
original_result.result: Tuned Adam reached 9.78 ± 0.25% test error, compared with 7.65 ± 0.14% for SGD.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Optimizer comparisons on explicitly identified models at 10–100B or above 100B parameters.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size and versions.V4.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size contain neither 10-100B nor >100B. The partials supply no identified comparison at these scales; unspecified sizes cannot establish coverage.

untested.what: An equal-budget restricted-versus-expanded tuning intervention that also reports paired training performance before and after expansion.
untested.basis: Choi's untested-parts line leaves the training-performance clause unestablished; Domain-Independent Dominance and Iterate Averaging identify controlled equal-budget tuning gaps. Their partial syntheses do not supply the complete joint comparison. counts: versions.V4.tested_with_controls and versions.V4.tested_with_uncertainty are aggregate fields and do not establish this joint design.

wording_issues.phrase: when only learning rates and decay schedules are tuned
wording_issues.issue: Learning-rate-only, schedule-tuned, default/shared-rate and broader searches are distinct conditions. Choi compares RMSProp and Adam with SGD and Momentum using grid-searched initial learning rates and a fixed decay schedule, selecting trials by validation performance rather than Wilson's training-based selection. Choi's schedule tuning alone equalizes CIFAR-10/VGG errors within error bars. Other comparisons additionally tune weight decay, momentum, epsilon or beta parameters and do not establish the stated restriction. The tuned-Adam CIFAR-10 results are selected grid maxima without displayed uncertainty; AlexNet's best beta2/epsilon-panel result differs from its learning-rate/epsilon-panel maximum.

The collection supplies selected, heterogeneous benchmark comparisons rather than a defined workload sampling frame. Verdict counts cannot estimate the prevalence of an adaptive-method penalty. Individually learning-rate-tuned CNN comparisons include condition-specific reversals favoring Adam, with significance unreported. Search-aggregated CPE comparisons favor Adam-LR over the listed SGD-MC variants on Fashion-MNIST and tie the highest listed SGD-MC value on CIFAR-100. Validation-selected CNN results also include an Adam advantage over the available SGD baseline. For VGG-16/CIFAR-10, the reported SGD-favoring interval is approximately 10^-3 ≤ α ≤ 10^(1/2), with Adam favored outside it; the upper crossover conflicts with the stated search range and high-rate results have greater uncertainty.

Adaptive algorithms are not interchangeable. Padam can approach SGD under broader tuning, spectrum-clipped Block-Adam can exceed momentum SGD, and layerwise or root-free methods avoid deficits found for ordinary Adam under their respective recipes. The Padam study also searches beta2 and changes the update rule; its results are descriptive coverage rather than tests of V4's restricted-tuning disadvantage. Adaptive-favorable ImageWoof10 comparisons under broad tuning are compatible with V4's existing qualification and do not establish that expanding the search caused the ordering. These comparisons require algorithm and recipe labels; they do not establish a uniform family-wide disadvantage.

wording_issues.phrase: sometimes despite equal or better training performance
wording_issues.issue: Paired training/held-out evidence supports this clause in particular settings, including Dissecting Adam, fully connected MNIST/CIFAR-10 and default ImageNet optimizers. In the fully connected MNIST comparison, Adam and SGD both attain 100% training accuracy, with test accuracies 98.22% and 98.44%, respectively. On CIFAR-10, Adam attains 99.89% training and 54.29% test accuracy; SGD attains 99.83% training and 55.98% test accuracy. Evaluation iterations for these reported accuracies are unstated; the first 1000 and 150 iterations describe early trajectory phases. Many other rows report held-out outcomes alone, and some deficits accompany worse training fit or underfitting. The clause should stay attached to measured training comparisons.

Different held-out metrics can reverse rankings: ImageNet accuracy and cross-entropy, CIFAR-10 accuracy and cross-entropy, clinical AUC and loss, and Top-1 versus Top-5 error need not agree. A single unspecified performance ordering loses these distinctions.

Final scores, best checkpoints, minimum test error, averaged peak validation accuracy and search-aggregated cumulative performance are different summaries. In ResNet34/CIFAR-10, AdaM exceeds SGD-StepLR at epoch 25 but trails it at epoch 250. The cited comparator cells are SGD-StepLR, not AdaBound; they provide no AdaBound checkpoint result. The early adaptive advantage is a condition-specific reversal of the predicted disadvantage. Linear-SVM evaluation of learned features and worst-group evaluation also require explicit qualification.

The comparator is consequential. In the cited Adam comparison, the disadvantage appears versus NAG and reverses versus SGDm; these are separate comparisons. On CIFAR-100/All-CNN-C with a large tuning budget and constant learning rate, AMSBound exceeds plain SGD but trails Momentum and NAG. This broader-tuned result does not contradict V4's existing qualification. Constant-step, scheduled and averaged SGD are additional distinctions. Comparisons that tune regularization or batch size do not establish the restricted-tuning condition. Full-batch GD, federated server algorithms and SGD-grafted methods require their own labels.

wording_issues.phrase: on word-level language models Adam can do better
wording_issues.issue: The qualification is supported, but adaptive advantages also occur in character modeling, translation, transformer pretraining and pretrained-model fine-tuning. Conversely, some word-level LSTM comparisons favor SGD, with rankings depending on depth, schedule and comparator. Token-level transformer results do not establish word-level tokenization.

wording_issues.phrase: Broader tuning can remove or reverse the difference
wording_issues.issue: Choi directly changes tuning protocols and observes equalization or reversal; its initial RMSProp/Adam versus SGD/Momentum comparison uses validation-selected initial learning rates with a fixed schedule, unlike Wilson's training-based trial selection. Under expanded CNN tuning, Adam outperforms Momentum, which outperforms SGD. Elsewhere, broader-tuned snapshots do not establish that expanding the search caused the rankings. The tuned-Adam CIFAR-10 evidence uses selected grid maxima without displayed uncertainty, with AlexNet's best result coming from the beta2/epsilon panel. Broadly tuned ImageWoof10 adaptive advantages fit V4's existing allowance. Persistent deficits after extensive tuning show that broader tuning is a conditional possibility rather than a sufficient remedy.

wording_issues.phrase: decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD can recover it
wording_issues.issue: Improvement over Adam, parity with SGD and improvement where Adam already wins are distinct outcomes. AdamW can retain an SGD deficit. SWATS temporarily reduces Tiny-ImageNet accuracy from 80% to 52% after switching, then reaches a peak above Adam; in language modeling it achieves comparable lowest validation perplexity to Adam, which outperforms SGD. These results do not establish a worse best SWATS result than Adam. The original reports provide remedy evidence, but recovery depends on workload and recipe; averaging, gradual transitions or AdamW-to-SGD hybrids do not isolate the stated interventions.

method_sensitivity.factor: Search space, search budget and optimizer parameters
method_sensitivity.what: Choi's limited search compares RMSProp and Adam with SGD and Momentum: initial learning-rate grid, fixed decay schedule, validation-based trial selection rather than Wilson's training-based selection. Schedule tuning alone removes the CIFAR-10/VGG separation; expanded tuning yields Adam above Momentum above SGD. Changing Adam beta1 removes the VGG-9 disadvantage. Another report's learning-rate/epsilon/beta2 grids yield selected accuracy maxima and perplexity minima without displayed uncertainty; AlexNet's best Adam accuracy comes from the beta2/epsilon panel. Calibrated random search depends on task, priors, tuned dimensions and budget; its early-weighted CPE differs from later-search rankings. CIFAR-100 CPE ties Adam-LR with SGD-MC, above SGD-MC WC and D. For a character RNN on Tolstoi's War and Peace, Adam-LR exceeds SGD-MC WC and D but trails Adam-WC D. Broader-tuned snapshots do not alone isolate search expansion.

method_sensitivity.factor: Learning rate, schedule and SGD momentum comparator
method_sensitivity.what: Adam can exceed SGDm yet trail NAG on the same CIFAR ResNet-18 experiments. Another comparison changes direction when a different plain-SGD learning rate or Nesterov comparator is selected. Fixed-rate versus MultiStep momentum SGD reverses its CIFAR-10 ordering against Adam. On ResNet-18/CIFAR-100, moderate fixed SGD momenta beat the best reported fixed Adam setting, whereas the largest tested momenta fall below it and also worsen training loss.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training duration, decay checkpoint and checkpoint aggregation
method_sensitivity.what: Early Adam/Amsgrad advantages in the Padam reproduction reverse at the final checkpoint. Block-cyclic epoch-segment averages can favor adaptive methods while final-epoch results favor SGD. ResNet56 peak-validation and late-epoch summaries produce different apparent deficits. The reported ImageNet ResNet-50 AdamW disadvantage shrinks with a longer training budget. These findings distinguish trajectory summaries, selected peaks and final performance.

method_sensitivity.factor: Weight-decay form and strength, normalization and augmentation
method_sensitivity.what: In VGG16/CIFAR-10 with Batch Normalization and no augmentation, SGD accuracy changes from 86.99% without weight decay to 88.85% with it, while Adam changes from 88.45% to 88.72%; ordering reverses. With augmentation on, SGD changes from 91.71% to 93.39%, Adam from 92.89% to 93.62%; Adam stays ahead. AdamW improves on Adam-L2 without Batch Normalization in another study; their best settings coincide with Batch Normalization because optimal decay is zero. At the lower-decay ResNet18/CIFAR-10 setting, test errors are AdamS 4.69%, AdamW 5.33%, SGD 5.58%, Adam 6.08%; Adam remains worse while AdamS/AdamW recover, consistent with V4's existing qualifications. Separate selected learning-rate/regularization settings improve AdamW over Adam-L2 without establishing SGD parity.

method_sensitivity.factor: Structure of adaptation, averaging and geometric constraints
method_sensitivity.what: Diagonal Adam, spectrum-clipped Block-Adam and SGD have different rankings; clipping and the late update rule modify the adaptive algorithm. AMSBound nominally reverses the disadvantage on DenseNet-BC-100-12/CIFAR-100: test error 22.17% versus SGD 22.27%, without reported uncertainty. Iterate averaging and partial adaptivity can recover deficits but not uniformly. Gadam's final ImageNet validation Top-1 accuracy is 76.79% versus SGD(step) 75.63%; its altered recipe uses initial learning rate 0.5, numerical stability coefficient 1 and weight decay 1E−4, with slower convergence. Increasing a continuous preconditioning exponent worsens CIFAR-100 accuracy and loss relative to its momentum-like zero setting. Verdict-only LAWN comparisons report recovery after switching to fixed-weight-norm training, with workload-dependent exceptions. These modifications do not isolate broader tuning alone.

method_sensitivity.factor: Task, architecture, depth and training stage
method_sensitivity.what: Adam is favored for BERT pretraining while SGD is favored for the accompanying ImageNet ResNet50 comparison. Noisy-label benchmarks favor momentum SGD on specified scratch-trained ResNets but AdamW on pretrained ViT fine-tuning. Penn Treebank LSTM depth changes Adam's ordering against momentum SGD. Neural ODE comparisons favor Adam on MNIST/CIFAR-10 and momentum SGD on SVHN. Architecture and training stage are not isolated from all accompanying recipe differences.

method_sensitivity.factor: Batch size, initialization and optimization stability
method_sensitivity.what: ALTO's CIFAR recipes favor SGD at small batches and adaptive baselines at large batches; budgets change from 200 to 400 epochs, so fixed-epoch batch effects are not isolated. Language-model sweeps favor Adam at larger batches and sufficiently long small-batch SGD at smaller batches; the deeper model retains this ordering. Figure 16 sequence length is inconsistent: Appendix A.2 says 1024, its caption 2048. ResNet-9 ordering reverses with initialization scale; its small-batch SGD recipe without warmup is unstable, with explicit kernel L2 regularization λ=5×10−4. Private WRN-16-4/CIFAR-10 at ε=4 shows no SGD advantage at batch 256 and a small SGD advantage at 4096. On SVHN at ε=4, batch 256 favors SGD despite appreciable seed variation. These are optimizer comparisons; within-batch comparisons alone do not establish V5.

method_sensitivity.factor: Held-out metric and conditioning on training fit
method_sensitivity.what: Default ImageNet Adam/NAdam lose on cross-entropy but exceed Heavy Ball/Nesterov on accuracy. CIFAR-10 ResNet18 Momentum has higher accuracy but worse cross-entropy than Adam/AdaHB in the PID study. Clinical adaptive methods can have worse validation cross-entropy but higher AUC. Subgroup fine-tuning can favor different optimizers on average and worst-group accuracy. Held-out scores, train–test gaps and comparisons conditioned on a common training loss are distinct measurements.

method_sensitivity.factor: Evaluation distribution, invariant features and data availability
method_sensitivity.what: Changing which CIFAR-10 feature spectrum remains invariant reverses OOD rankings: SGD is favored with invariant top principal components, while K-FAC is favored with invariant bottom noise. Seismic validation metrics favor Adam on synthetic data, whereas real-data transfer favors momentum SGD. Matrix-completion GD–Adam differences narrow with greater sampling density and with held-out rather than training-only learning-rate selection. Spurious-feature correlation strength and subgroup evaluation also change the observed comparison.

method_sensitivity.factor: Switch timing, optimizer role and distributed-training recipe
method_sensitivity.what: SWATS can initially reduce image accuracy before reaching a better peak, or preserve already superior Adam language-model performance. The DualAdam comparison reports lower SWATS mean accuracy in specified CNN and CIFAR-10 ViT settings but an improvement on CIFAR-100 ViT; switching-rate extremes degrade performance. PALSGD's verdict favors AdamW as inner optimizer but penalizes it as outer optimizer. Federated server ordering reverses between heterogeneous and homogeneous CIFAR-100 partitions. The PALSGD and partition comparisons are verdict-only findings.
